speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing persistent bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction and a history of easy bruising. To understand if this is a bleeding disorder, have you noticed any excessive bleeding during this procedure, and do you experience nosebleeds or bleeding gums spontaneously?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia B (Factor IX deficiency). The patient's presentation of delayed post-extraction bleeding, easy bruising, and a family history involving an uncle with similar symptoms and joint swelling (hemarthrosis) strongly suggests an X-linked recessive bleeding disorder. While Hemophilia A is statistically more common, the specific inclusion of joint swelling in the family history warrants a targeted workup for both Factor VIII and Factor IX levels, with Hemophilia B being a primary consideration given the "similar issues" description in the uncle. I will proceed to request coagulation studies to confirm the specific factor deficiency.

REQUEST TEST: PT/INR, aPTT, Factor VIII activity, Factor IX activity.
REQUEST IMAGES: None required at this stage; laboratory confirmation is the priority.
